title: The equation of centre is the angle at the sun, with tan c = e sin κ̄ / (R + e cos κ̄)
author: Gerd Graßhoff

variables.name: kappa_bar
variables.meaning: mean anomaly about E, counted from the apogee

observables.name: c
observables.meaning: equation of centre, mean minus true longitude

constructions.name: F
constructions.meaning: foot of the perpendicular from the earth on ES

argument.claim: OE produced to the apogee: the exterior angle at E of the triangle OES
argument.formal: equal(angle(S, E, A), angle(E, S, O) + angle(S, O, E))

by.statement: In any triangle, if one of the sides be produced, the exterior angle is equal to the two interior and opposite angles, and the three interior angles of the triangle are equal to two right angles.

argument.note: configuration conditions fail there: noncollinear(S, O, E)
conditions: O, E, A on one line

argument.claim: the exterior angle is κ̄ and the angle at O is κ, so the angle at S is κ̄ − κ = c

by.statement: The proposition follows from the cited equalities by calculation.
The proposition is read off the cited constructions: it holds for every parameter value and every state without any hypothesis.

argument.formal: equal(distance(O, F), distance(O, E) * sin(angle(O, E, F)))

by.statement: In a right triangle the side opposite an acute angle is the hypotenuse times the sine of that angle.

argument.note: configuration conditions fail there: distinct(E, F), distinct(O, F)
conditions: E, S, F on one line

by.statement: The proposition is read off the cited constructions: it holds for every parameter value and every state without any hypothesis.

argument.claim: the angle OEF is κ̄ or its supplement, according to the side of E on which F falls

by.statement: The proposition is read off the cited constructions: it holds for every parameter value and every state without any hypothesis.
The proposition follows from the cited equalities by calculation.

argument.claim: F lies on SE produced beyond E for κ̄ within 90° of the apogee, between S and E otherwise: SF = SE ± EF

by.statement: The proposition is read off the cited constructions: it holds for every parameter value and every state without any hypothesis.

argument.formal: equal(tan(angle(O, S, F)), distance(O, F) / distance(S, F))

by.statement: In a right triangle the tangent of an acute angle is the opposite side over the adjacent side.

argument.note: configuration conditions fail there: distinct(O, F)
conditions: S, E, F on one line

argument.claim: F and E lie from S on one ray
argument.formal: equal(angle(O, S, F), angle(O, S, E))

by.statement: The proposition is read off the cited constructions: it holds for every parameter value and every state without any hypothesis.

argument.formal: equal(distance(O, F), distance(O, S) * sin(angle(O, S, F)))

by.statement: In a right triangle the side opposite an acute angle is the hypotenuse times the sine of that angle.

argument.note: configuration conditions fail there: distinct(O, F)
conditions: S, E, F on one line

argument.formal: equal(distance(O, S) * distance(O, S), distance(O, F) * distance(O, F) + distance(S, F) * distance(S, F))

by.statement: In right-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the right angle is equal to the squares on the sides containing the right angle.

argument.note: configuration conditions fail there: distinct(O, F)
conditions: S, E, F on one line

conclusion.claim: tan c = e sin κ̄ / (R + e cos κ̄), in absolute value

by.statement: The proposition follows from the cited equalities by calculation.

further_conclusions.claim: sin c = e sin κ̄ / (R² + e² + 2Re cos κ̄)^½, in absolute value
further_conclusions.formal: equal(sin(abs(norm180(c))), e * abs(sin(kappa_bar)) / sqrt(R * R + e * e + 2 * R * e * cos(kappa_bar)))

by.statement: The proposition follows from the cited equalities by calculation.

notes: d2 rests on the stated proposition p1 (equal(lam_bar, lamA + kappa_bar)), which is checked numerically, not derived
d2 rests on the stated proposition p2 (equal(kappa, kappa_bar - c)), which is checked numerically, not derived

degenerate states, in which a step's rule does not apply, a term is undefined or an inequality becomes an equality: kappa_bar = 0°; kappa_bar = 180°; kappa_bar = 270°; kappa_bar = 90°. The derivation does not cover them; the conclusion is true there as well (numerically)
